Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13
November, 2024 
 1
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal Nos.420, 546, 743 of 2008,
 945 of 2009 and 718 Of 2010
Common Judgment :
1. Criminal Appeal No.420 of 2008 is filed by A2, Criminal Appeal No.546 of 2008 is filed by A6,
Criminal Appeal No.743 of 2008 is filed by A4 & A8, Criminal Appeal No.945 of 2009 is filed by A5,
Criminal Appeal No.718 of 2008 is filed by A7. Since all the appellants are arrayed as accused,
challenging the judgment in S.C.No.156 of 2007, dated 28.03.2008, they are being disposed off by way of this common judgment. 
2. The appellants/A2 and A4 were convicted under Section 366 IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years, further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years under Section 376(2)(g) r/w 109 IPC, further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years under Section 366 IPC and further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years under Section 4 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years under Section 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act. A5 to A8 are sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years under Section 376(2)(g) IPC. Aggrieved by the said conviction, present appeals are filed. 
3. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that a complaint was filed by P.W.2, a social worker on 28.09.2006 to register case against 8 persons for offences committed against a minor girl (PW1).
According to the complaint, PW1, who had lost her parents, was being looked after by her brother,
who sold chips at the CBS Bus Stand in Hyderabad. He enrolled her in a hostel in Hyderabad, where she studied until the 10th grade. Later, he told P.W.1 that he would take her to Bangalore, and took her to Secunderabad Railway Station. Around 8:00 pm, he left the station to get food but did not return, causing PW1 to panic as it was already midnight. A2, A3, and A4, approached PW1, sat next to her, and befriended her. They advised her against sitting alone for her safety and offered her a job with a monthly salary of Rs 2,500 and also tailoring lessons. They took her in an auto to a place in Sai Nagar, Kushaiguda. Further, on the same day, around 4:00pm, A2 asked her to dress up, stating she would take her to a garment shop, but instead brought her back to Secunderabad Railway Station and made her stand in one spot. When PW1 questioned A2, she was told to remain silent. 
After sometime, a person approached and A2 negotiated a price of Rs 2,500 for one night,
threatening PW1 by stating that he was a policeman, forcing her compliance. Said person along with four friends, took her to an unknown location wherein she was assaulted and raped. 
Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26548742/
1 4. P.W.1 was taken back to Kushaiguda, where she was allegedly gang-raped by A2's associates,
including A5, A6, A7, and A8. Thereafter, she was repeatedly brought to Secunderabad Railway Station and forced into sexual acts with multiple men. P.W.1 escaped after being taken by some college boys to a different location, from where she fled to the CBS Bus Stand. 
5. On 13.07.2006, the Afzalgunj Rescue Team rescued PW1 and placed her in a shelter home run by PW2, the General Secretary of 'Prajwala' Organization, a social organization, which focuses on anti-trafficking efforts. Due to trauma, PW1 was initially unable to discuss her ordeal, however, after two months, she gained the confidence to disclose what had happened. A formal complaint was then filed on her behalf by P.W.2 and she was sent for medical examination to confirm her age and gather evidence of sexual exploitation. The police concluded investigation and filed charge sheet arraying A1 to A10. Case against A1 & A9 was split up. 
6. The trial Court framed charges against A2 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Sections 366 and 506 IPC, Sections 3, 4 and 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, A5 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) IPC, A2 to A4 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) r/w 109 IPC.
7. During the course of trial, learned Sessions Judge examined P.Ws.1 to 9 and marked Exs.P1 to P19 and the vehicles which were used to take victim girl were marked as MOs.1 to 5. A10 examined two witnesses D.Ws.1 and 2. Learned Sessions Judge having considered the evidence on record convicted the appellants as stated supra while acquitting A10. Further, the Sessions Judge found that as on the date of offence, victim girl was not a minor. 
8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants argued that the testimony of PW1 contains numerous inconsistencies. The prosecution did not clarify which police station initially registered the crime. According to PW1, she was rescued by the Afzalgunj Police, under Charminar PS's jurisdiction, making the Gopalpuram PS's registration of the crime inexplicable. PW2 allegedly influenced Gopalpuram Police due to her ongoing connections with them through her organization. 
Counsel submits that there is no documentation proving PW2's organization's legitimacy, nor was a referral report for PW1's placement in PW2's rescue home filed. P.W.1 allegedly leads an immoral lifestyle and was not raped, as she admitted to having paid fines on various occasions, though the police constable involved was unnamed. PW1's statement of intending to travel to Bangalore is implausible, as she has no known relations there. PW1 did not file a complaint regarding her brother's disappearance. Counsel further submits that if the brother of P.W.1, was selling chips at the bus stand, the police should have been able to locate him, yet the prosecution provided no explanation for his absence. The owner of the house where PW1 was allegedly kept was not called to testify. PW1's age certificate could have been obtained from her school, as she had studied up to the 10th class. P.W.1's relatives were not summoned as witnesses. No test identification parade was conducted for PW1 to identify the appellants. The appellant's surname is missing in Exhibit P8. PW1 reportedly made no effort to attract the attention of passers-by. Despite evidence of signboards at the railway station, PW1 did not attempt to inform anyone there. PW2, the complainant, allegedly lacks the locus standi to file the complaint. 
Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26548742/
2 9. On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor argued on behalf of the State stating that hapless victim/P.W.1 was subjected to rape and she was forced to become a prostitute whereby A2 to A4 were the pimps and A5 to A8 had mercilessly raped her. In the said circumstances, appellants conviction is proper. 
10. Having gone through the record, learned Sessions Judge has correctly found that the victim was not a minor when the incident has taken place. 
11. The allegation of committing gang rape by A5 to A8 at the instance of A2 to A4 is on the basis of testimony of P.W.1 who stated that when P.W.1 wanted to go to Bangalore, A2 to A4 asked her and informed that they would secure a room and get her job. She was taken to Radhika Theater,
Sainagar, Kushaiguda where A5 to A8 and A10 raped her. The other instance narrated by P.W.1 is that after considerable period of the alleged rape, the traffic police on Tankbund Police Station took her to the Police Station. Then the police let her go after she paid some amount and then she returned to room near Radhika Theater and wanted to escape from A2 to A4. However, her attempts to escape did not succeed and A2 to A4 beat her. When she tried to escape from the police station,
one police constable had taken her and handed over to A2 to A4. At the instance of A2to A4, A5 to A10 raped her. 
12. The said two instances narrated by P.W.1 form basis for the learned Sessions Judge to record conviction for gang rape against A5 to A8 and abetting gang rape by A2 to A4. 
13. The version of A10 that he was not present, was believed by the learned Sessions Judge and he was acquitted. No reasons are given as to why the learned Sessions Judge has not believed P.W.1 selectively regarding rape by A10 and accepted the version of P.W.1 that she was raped by A5 to A8. 
It is not in dispute that the police failed to identify the place of the alleged rape which was in a room near Radhika Theater. P.W.1 has not shown the place where the alleged gang rape had taken place. 
14. According to P.W.1, she was in Hyderabad till the date of lodging complaint on 28.09.2006. In her examination in chief before the Court below her date of birth is not given nor the approximate year was stated though she studied till 10th class and stayed in a hostel at Hyderabad. Thereafter,
her brother wanted to take her to Bangalore and took her to Railway Station and left her there stating that he would get food but did not return. Then A2 to A4 came there and took her to room at Kushaiguda. 
15. According to the complaint Ex.P1, P.W.1 came to Hyderabad in December, 2005 and the alleged luring by A2 to A4 was in December, 2005. What happened from December, 2005 to December,
2006 was not specifically stated in the complaint. However, narration is given that A2 to A4 were bringing customers and she was catering to the customers. Even in the complaint Ex.P1, it is no where stated as to when A5 to A8 committed gang rape. Learned Sessions Judge, while discussing the evidence noted that there was lack of evidence against A5 to A8 and also against A10 regarding sexual acts with P.W.1. However, it does not affect the case of gang rape. As already stated A10 was acquitted by disbelieving the evidence of P.W.1 that A10 also raped her along with A5 to A8. The offence of gang rape is serious offence and the vague manner in which the allegation is made against Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26548742/ 
3 A5 to A8 and A10 regarding their alleged sexual assault and gang rape on two occasions cannot form basis to convict them for the said offence in the absence of P.W.1 identifying the place where the incident happened. P.W.1 stayed in Hyderabad along with A2 to A4 for over 10 months before lodging the complaint. P.W.1 also stayed in a hostel in Hyderabad till she completed her 10th class. 
The said school was not identified during investigation. Though, from the evidence of P.W.1 it can be gathered that A2 to A4 were getting several customers every day over a period of 10 months, in the absence of proof of forcible raping P.W.1 only on the basis of bald allegations regarding committing gang rape, the evidence does not inspire confidence to sustain the conviction under Section 376(2)(g) of IPC.
16. P.W.1 stated that she was taken by A2 to A4 on the premise that she would be offered a job with Rs.2,500/- salary and went there. However, it is unclear as to why P.W.1 had never lodged any complaint at any point of time for the period of ten months while she was going around the city. 
According to her either customers were brought to the place where she was living or she was taken to several hotels and other places. P.W.1 also admitted that on three occasions she was arrested by the police and was let off after paying some amount to them. P.W.1 admittedly had never complained to the police regarding her plight to anybody. In fact, according to her, she gave money to the police to wriggle out of the situation of police for detaining her for practicing prostitution. 
17. Section 4 and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act reads as follows:
"4. Punishment for living on the earnings of prostitution.--
(1) Any person over the age of eighteen years who knowingly lives, wholly or in part,
on the earnings of the prostitution of 1 [any other person] shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both 2 [and where such earnings relate to the prostitution of a child or a minor, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term of not less than seven years and not more than ten years].
3 [(2) Where any person over the age of eighteen years is proved-- (a) to be living with, or to be habitually in the company of, a prostitute; or (b) to have exercised control, direction or influence over the movements of a prostitute in such a manner as to show that such person is aiding, abetting or compelling her prostitution; or (c) to be acting as a tout or pimp on behalf of a prostitute, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that such person is knowingly living on the earnings of prostitution of another person within the meaning of sub-section (1).]
5. Procuring, inducing or taking 4 [person] for the sake of prostitution.--(1) any person who-- Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26548742/
4 (a) procures or attempts to procure a 4 [person], whether with or without his consent, for the purpose of prostitution; or (b) induces a 4 [person] to go from any place, with the intent that he may for the purpose of prostitution become the inmate of, or frequent, a brothel; or (c) takes or attempts to take a 4 [person], or causes a 4 [person] to be taken, from one place to another with a view to his carrying on, or being brought up to carry on prostitution; or (d) causes or induces a [person] to carry on prostitution;
[shall be punishable on conviction with rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than three years and not more than seven years and also with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees and if any offence under this sub-section is committed against the will of any person, the punishment of imprisonment for a term of seven years shall extend to imprisonment for a term of fourteen years:
Provided that if the person in respect of whom an offence committed under this sub-section,--
(i) is a child, the punishment provided under this sub-section shall extend to rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than seven years but may extend to life; and (ii) is a minor, the punishment provided under this sub-section shall extend to rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than seven years and not more than fourteen years;] (3) An offence under this section shall be triable-- (a) in the place from which a 1 [person] is procured, induced to go, taken or caused to be taken or from which an attempt to procure or take such 1 [person] is made; or (b) in the place to which he may have gone as a result of the inducement or to which he is taken or caused to be taken or an attempt to take him is made."
18. In the said circumstances, offence under Section 366, 376(2)(g) r/w 109 of IPC are not made out against A2 and A4. Further offences under Section 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act is also not made out. A5 to A8 are found not guilty for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) IPC. However,
conviction under Section 4 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act is retained against A2 and A4 19. Accordingly, Criminal Appeal No.420 of 2008 is partly allowed, Criminal Appeal Nos.546 of 2008, 945 of 2009, 718 of 2010 are allowed and Criminal Appeal No.743 of 2008 is concerned, it is partly allowed against A4 and allowed against A8.

on 13
November, 2024

 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal Nos.420, 546, 743 of 2008,
 945 of 2009 and 718 Of 2010

summary.facts:
2. The appellants/A2 and A4 were convicted under Section 366 IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years, further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years under Section 376(2)(g) r/w 109 IPC, further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years under Section 366 IPC and further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years under Section 4 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years under Section 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
5. On 13.07.2006, the Afzalgunj Rescue Team rescued PW1 and placed her in a shelter home run by PW2, the General Secretary of 'Prajwala' Organization, a social organization, which focuses on anti-trafficking efforts.
A formal complaint was then filed on her behalf by P.W.2 and she was sent for medical examination to confirm her age and gather evidence of sexual exploitation.
The police concluded investigation and filed charge sheet arraying A1 to A10.
Case against A1 & A9 was split up.
6. The trial Court framed charges against A2 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Sections 366 and 506 IPC, Sections 3, 4 and 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, A5 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) IPC, A2 to A4 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) r/w 109 IPC.
7.
summary.arguments: On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor argued on behalf of the State stating that hapless victim/P.W.1 was subjected to rape and she was forced to become a prostitute whereby A2 to A4 were the pimps and A5 to A8 had mercilessly raped her.
summary.ANALYSIS:
In the said circumstances, appellants conviction is proper.
When she tried to escape from the police station,
one police constable had taken her and handed over to A2 to A4.
At the instance of A2to A4, A5 to A10 raped her.
However, it does not affect the case of gang rape.
The offence of gang rape is serious offence and the vague manner in which the allegation is made against Dudekula Jaya, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 13 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26548742/
The said school was not identified during investigation.
Though, from the evidence of P.W.1 it can be gathered that A2 to A4 were getting several customers every day over a period of 10 months, in the absence of proof of forcible raping P.W.1 only on the basis of bald allegations regarding committing gang rape, the evidence does not inspire confidence to sustain the conviction under Section 376(2)(g) of IPC.
16.
summary.decision:
In the said circumstances, offence under Section 366, 376(2)(g) r/w 109 of IPC are not made out against A2 and A4.
Further offences under Section 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act is also not made out.
A5 to A8 are found not guilty for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) IPC.
However,
conviction under Section 4 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act is retained against A2 and A4 19.
Accordingly, Criminal Appeal No.420 of 2008 is partly allowed, Criminal Appeal Nos.546 of 2008, 945 of 2009, 718 of 2010 are allowed and Criminal Appeal No.743 of 2008 is concerned, it is partly allowed against A4 and allowed against A8.
